newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares cede early gains to close weaker.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares cede early gains to close weaker.

text.p: Dutch shares ended on the defensive on Wednesday after data showing a burgeoning U.S. trade gap hit the dollar and markets across Europe.
The AEX index of leading shares closed 1.11 points down at 563.16 in the middle of the day's 561.06 to 565.16 range.
The Dutch market started the day firmly but in the absence of strong investor buying, option market makers were able to sell the market lower and quickly reverse the trend.
Dealers said option grantors were keen to keep the index below the key 565 point level and so prevent a large volume of contracts being exercised at the expiry due on Friday.
Dealers said this could take the index as low as 560 but keeping it below 565 was the crucial thaing. However, after the expiry, the market could take off, they added.
"We feel we are going to fly after the weeekend," one brokers note said.
Among individual stocks, the turnaround in Heineken shares lost steam but the brewer still ended one guilder firmer at 306.
Philips was among the few gainers as interest in the stock continued after positive comments from U.S. semi-conducter maker Intel sparked buying on Tuesday.
